notes: διὰ χειρὸς αὐτῶν is rendered by them: διά takes by, αὐτῶν takes them, and χειρός is unrepresented, no English word answering to it.
The italicized thus is folded onto γράψαντες under rule 103's licensing test; reading it added under rule 86 stays defensible and is recorded in the unit's note.

τοῖς … ἀδελφοῖς τοῖς ἐξ ἐθνῶν follows rules 31 and 57: the preceding article takes unto the across the interposed prepositional phrase, the noun takes brethren, the following article keeps only who, and ἐξ carries the supplied copula as are of.
